email_subject: Application - Marketplace PPC / Performance Marketing Role (Antwerp)
email_body:
Dear Loop team,

I'm applying for the marketplace PPC role in Antwerp. I've spent the last few years in digital marketing where paid search, e-commerce and measurement meet: Google Ads Search and GA4 certified, working daily with Google Analytics and Search Console, and building and running Shopify and WooCommerce stores from store design through product catalogue. Product pages and retail readiness aren't abstractions to me.

I don't yet own Amazon or Bol campaigns day to day - my paid experience sits mainly in Google Ads - but the metric family is one I already read: spend, impressions, CTR, CPC, conversion rate, ROAS. I'd rather learn your platforms inside your playbook than pretend otherwise. What I bring is a technical, structured way of working: Python automation for the repetitive parts, and the habit of raising a pacing risk early instead of in a monthly report.

A 7 December start works for me.

cover_letter:
Dear Loop team,

Your posting says Loopers step in, speak up and go all in. That's the part I recognised. I've spent the past few years in digital marketing where paid search, e-commerce and measurement meet, and I want my next move to be real ownership of marketplace advertising rather than another seat on the sidelines.

My foundation is PPC and performance marketing. I'm Google Ads Search and GA4 certified, work daily in Google Analytics and Search Console, and have built and maintained Shopify and WooCommerce stores end to end: store design, product catalogues, product-page content, blog. That's the unglamorous side of e-commerce, and it's the part that decides whether an ad can perform at all. I know what a weak product page does to conversion rate, and I'd rather flag it early than watch spend drain.

I'm also technical in a way that helps here: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, a front-end background building a healthcare web application at ViviDoctor, structured data and JSON-LD work, and Python automation for repetitive reporting. I use LLMs daily for research, content and audits, and I've shipped an Android app to Google Play on my own. When something needs building, I build it.

What I don't have is day-to-day Amazon Seller Central or Bol campaign ownership; my paid experience sits mainly in Google Ads. The signals are familiar - spend, CTR, CPC, conversion rate, ACOS, ROAS - and I'd come into your playbook to learn the platforms properly instead of guessing.

I work structured and detail-oriented, follow through on what I own, and ask sharp questions early. A 7 December start works for me, and Zwijndrecht to Antwerp is a short commute. Thank you for your time.
